transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I suppose I'm just... always up and moving around. Even on a quiet day, I'm... I'm bouncing from my garden club list to my knitting bag, or looking at travel papers. I just... I don't really finish any one thing before I'm on to the next.
Has this tendency to bounce between tasks been something you have experienced since childhood?

Yes, I suppose so. My mother... well, she used to say my teachers thought I was smart enough, just... scattered. I guess I lost my schoolwork a lot. And they'd say I talked when I shouldn't, or couldn't sit still long enough to finish an assignment. It's just always been that way.
Do you often find yourself struggling with persistent worry about everyday things that feels difficult to control?
No... not really. I mean, I worry sometimes, like anyone else, I suppose. But it's not... it doesn't take over my days or anything.
Do these challenges cause noticeable difficulties in your everyday routine or responsibilities?

Well... yes, I suppose it does. It's... it's been causing some strain lately. At home, and over at the community center. My husband and the other volunteers... they feel like they can't really count on me to keep plans straight. Not unless someone is, well, checking up behind me.

inference_history.note: Initial presentation of restlessness, distractibility, and multi-tasking without finishing tasks suggests ADHD, hypomania/bipolar affective disorder, or generalized anxiety disorder.

Childhood-onset, chronic inattention, motor restlessness, and impulsivity make episodic mood disorders (F30.0, F31.0) unlikely, leaving ADHD (F90.0) as the primary candidate, with GAD (F41.1) to be formally ruled out.
